newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU member states split on farm price cuts.
newsitem.headline: EU member states split on farm price cuts.

text.p: A majority of European Union member states remain hostile to proposed cuts in aid for cereal and sugar storage or compensation for flax and hemp growers, an EU member state official said on Wednesday.
"There seems little likelihood that there will be any agreement in advance of the next farm council in two weeks time," the official said.
The official reported "almost no progress" at Tuesday's EU special agriculture committee on the cuts proposed by the European Commission as part of its annual farm prices package.
Ministers are due to consider the package again at their next meeting in Luxembourg on April 21.

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler put forward a plan at the March farm ministers' meeting to reduce monthly intervention storage payments by nine percent to 1.0 Ecu a tonne to take account of lower interest rates.

Flax and hemp area aid payments would be cut by the proposal by 5.7 percent to 815.86 Ecus per hectare and by 7.5 percent to 716.63 Ecus per hectare. A flax promotional levy of 49.62 Ecus per hectare would be reduced to zero.
In addition the Commissioner proposed a reduction in the monthly sugar storage refund by 17 percent to 0.35 Ecu per 100 kg, also reflecting lower interest rates.

Discussion at the special agriculture committee focused on these issues but the official commented: "It is clear from the meeting that the majority of member states would rather not make cuts in the monthly cereal and sugar storage rates." -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
